An Ansarallah drone struck the Public Investment Fund (PIF) Tower - the tallest building in Riyadh - injuring 11 people. The 365-metre skyscraper is home to Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund. The Saudi-led Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Maliki vowed a "resolute response". This is the second time this tower has been struck. Interestingly, no alerts were issued for Riyadh during this attack, which indicates Saudi Arabia is pursuing a policy of censorship, creating the illusion of fewer Ansrallah attacks.

Yemen’s Foreign Ministry in Sanaa warned that any hostile British action harming the Yemeni people would be met with a reciprocal response. The ministry said the hostile British measures were intended to legitimize the Saudi regime’s daily crimes in Yemen. It described the move as a blatant step taken after Saudi Arabia’s failure to occupy Yemen and deprive it of its freedom and independence. The ministry added that the anniversary of the expulsion of the last British occupier from Yemen reaffirms that projects aimed at control, hegemony, colonialism, and the confiscation of freedoms are gone forever. Addressing Saudi Arabia, it stressed that Britain and other parties would not help Riyadh overcome its current predicament, saying the only solution was to end the aggression against Yemen and lift the siege.

Following Ansarallah's attack in the Public Investment Fund (PIF) Tower in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia issued evacuation orders for Al-Hudaydah Port in Yemen. In response to this, Ansarallah issued their own evacuation orders for Saudi Arabia's Jazan, Yanbu, King Fahd, and Jeddah Ports, stating that they will carry out attacks on them if Saudi Arabia strikes Al-Hudaydah Port.
